title: Final balloon volume
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (1) must be expressed as ((1-k)/k) * v1 or an equivalent algebraic form.

title: Final gas pressure
description: Essential: The student's final answer for part (2) must be expressed as (k * p1 * T2) / T1 or an equivalent algebraic form.

title: Apply Boyle's Law
description: Important: The solution for part (1) must correctly apply Boyle's Law (pV = constant at constant temperature) to the initial and final states at T1.

title: Apply Charles's/Gay-Lussac's Law
description: Important: The solution for part (2) must correctly apply the pressure-temperature law (p/T = constant at constant volume) to the sealed balloon's ascent.

title: Define total system volume
description: Important: For part (1), the reasoning must account for the total final volume (V1 + V_balloon) when the pressure becomes k*p1.

title: Recognize constant volume
description: Optional: The solution may explicitly state that the balloon volume is constant after sealing for the ascent in part (2).

title: Incorrect gas law application
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses the ideal gas law on a changing mass of gas in part (1) instead of a mass-conserving Boyle's Law argument.

title: Sign or algebraic error
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the algebra for part (1) yields an incorrect sign (e.g., (k-1)/k) or misplaces the factor k.
